    Colors
    The map legend shows what the colors mean for the selected layer. Zero marks the historical baseline in an anomaly view.
    Trend line
    Shows the general climate trend for the years you select. With none selected, it fits the measured record.
    Significant
    The trend meets Atlas’s 5% cutoff for evidence of change. How we test trends.
    Projected
    A statistical estimate that extends the recent trend to 2100. The shaded range shows how much the estimate can vary. How projections work.

          Correlation, r

          —

          r runs from −1 to +1, and values near 0 mean no straight-line relationship. Two variables that both rise over the decades correlate even if neither affects the other; removing the trend checks for that. A correlation does not show cause.

          Why this matters

          The world’s average hides the places changing fastest. Plans for heat, water, crops and ice are made locally, so the local record is the one that counts.

          Read why

          What you can do

          Compare your city with a faster-changing place, check whether its trend is significant, and share the chart or data with people who make local decisions.
